note: Outbound license recommendations by goal: CounselMode editorial view, not legal advice. choose() and references/choosing-a-license.md are both built from this file.

goals.title: Maximum adoption, including by companies

candidates.note: adds an express patent grant and contribution terms

goals.why: Minimal friction; Apache-2.0 adds an express patent grant and contribution terms
goals.trade_offs: Others can build proprietary forks without giving back

goals.title: Keep your library improvements open, allow proprietary apps to use it

candidates.note: library-level copyleft; users must be able to relink

goals.trade_offs: LGPL relinking requirements can deter mobile/embedded use; MPL is simpler

goals.title: Ensure all derivative distributions remain open
goals.why: Strong copyleft with patent and anti-tivoization terms
goals.trade_offs: Many companies avoid embedding GPL code

goals.title: Prevent cloud providers from offering your software as a service without contributing
goals.why: AGPL stays open source; source-available gives stronger protection but is not open source
goals.trade_offs: AGPL reduces enterprise adoption; source-available triggers community backlash and forks

goals.title: Monetize with dual licensing
goals.why: Copyleft pushes commercial users to buy a license
goals.trade_offs: Contributors must sign a CLA so you can relicense their work; community friction

candidates.note: for non-code works: it excludes patent rights, so prefer 0BSD or MIT-0 for code

goals.title: Release model weights openly

not_open_source.note: if you want use restrictions; use-restricted licenses are not open source

goals.trade_offs: Use-restricted licenses are not open source

goals.title: Release a dataset
goals.why: Clear rights for training and reuse
goals.trade_offs: Share-alike data licenses (ODbL, CC-BY-SA) complicate downstream use
